::: {.statx-chapter-banner}
## From rows and columns to a statistical story

This lab will turn an unfamiliar dataset into a clear description of its variables, observations, center, spread, and shape.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

1. Classify variables as categorical or numerical, and numerical variables as discrete or continuous.
2. Distinguish a population, a sample, a parameter, and a statistic.
3. Calculate and compare measures of center and variability.
4. Select and interpret an appropriate histogram, boxplot, or bar chart.

## Planned workflow

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 1. Meet the data

Build a compact data dictionary and identify the observational unit for every row.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 2. Summarize

Compute counts, proportions, mean, median, range, variance, standard deviation, and quartiles where appropriate.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 3. Visualize

Create distribution plots and examine how bin width, scale, and outliers affect the message.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 4. Communicate

Write a short results paragraph that connects numerical summaries to visible patterns.
:::
:::

## Deliverables

- A data dictionary with variable types
- One numerical-summary table
- Two purposeful visualizations
- A concise interpretation in complete sentences
